html:
At Hafrsfjord, near Stavanger, a sea battle in about 872 is said to have made Harald Fairhair the first king of all Norway.

The sagas, written in Iceland three centuries later by writers such as Snorri Sturluson, tell that Harald swore not to cut his hair until he ruled the whole country, and that he beat the last of the western chieftains here. Modern historians think his rule was real but smaller, mostly along the west coast.

The sagas also say that chieftains who would not bow to him left for Iceland, which helps explain the settlement of Iceland. Whatever its true size, the battle stands in Norwegian memory as the founding of the kingdom. A monument of three swords stands at the site.
sum: At Hafrsfjord, near Stavanger, a sea battle in about 872 is said to have made Harald Fairhair the first king of all Norway.
